subject: religion
title: Faith and Morality in Islam
summary: Fundamental beliefs of Islam and moral teachings for daily life

sections.title: The Six Pillars of Faith (Iman)
sections.content: In Islam, there are six pillars of faith: (1) Belief in Allah, (2) Belief in angels, (3) Belief in the revealed books (including the Quran, Injil, Torah, Zabur), (4) Belief in the prophets (from Adam to Muhammad), (5) Belief in the Day of Judgment, (6) Belief in divine destiny (Qadr). These beliefs form the foundation of a Muslim's faith.

sections.title: The Five Pillars of Islam
sections.content: The Five Pillars are the framework of Muslim life: (1) Shahada - declaring there is no god but Allah and Muhammad is His messenger, (2) Salat - praying five times daily, (3) Zakat - giving charity to those in need, (4) Sawm - fasting during the month of Ramadan, (5) Hajj - pilgrimage to Makkah at least once in a lifetime if able.

sections.title: Moral Values in Islam
sections.content: Islam teaches many moral values: honesty (amanah), truthfulness (sidq), kindness (rahma), respect for parents and elders, helping the poor and orphans, cleanliness (tahara), and justice (adl). The Prophet Muhammad said: 'The best among you are those who have the best manners and character.'

sections.title: Daily Islamic Practices
sections.content: Muslim children should learn to: recite Bismillah before any action, say Alhamdulillah after completing something, use the right hand for eating and giving, greet others with Assalamu Alaikum, respect teachers and parents, keep themselves and their surroundings clean, and be truthful in all dealings.
